To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We present an efficient search algorithm for materials discovery using evolutionary algorithms (EAs) coupled with machine learned surrogate models.

we developed an evolutionary algorithm powered by machine learning surrogate models that enables the efficient search over a chemical space of 1011 quatenary compounds for candidates with target optical properties.
We present a machine learned approach to materials discovery that is able to efficiently explore the materials space and discover new materials with specific target properties (Figure 2a).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a machine learned framework for accelerated materials design and discovery of new UV light emitters (Supplementary Figure S11 for the bandgap distribution of the materials in our dataset) The framework is composed of two parts.
the discovery of new semimetal and semiconductors for light harvesting, sensing, lases and energy storage.
developing a ML based search algorithm for efficient and interpretable discovery of materials with specific targeted optical properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ML based bandgap predictions are in good agreement with experiments and can be used to guide the experiments in materials discovery.
ML models trained on DFT data are able to accurately predict HSE bandgaps and directindirect nature, and can be used to efficiently search over the materials chemical space.
GCNNs are capable of learning the bandgap and the nature of bandgapes of a wide range of compounds with high accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our models trained on DFT data predict HSE06 energies with an MAE of 1.2 eV/atom, and HSE06 bandgap with MAE of ~0.5 eV, and the direct/indrect bandgap nature with F1 score of ~0.8.

we developed an accurate and efficient ML framework for predicting the bandgap and nature of the bandgap of the materials and we use this framework in an evolutionary algorithm to accelerate the discovery of novel materials.
the GCNN models are trained on a dataset that is generated using high throughput DFT calculations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GCNN model is able to predict the HSE06 bandgap and the directindirect classification of the material with high accuracy and is able to reproduce DFT values with a MAE of 1.1 eV.
the bandgap prediction and direct/indirect classification are possible using ML models trained on DFT bandgaps.
the ML models trained on HSE bandgaps can be used to guide experimental materials synthesis.
